title: Verifier‑Assisted vs. LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with up to one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation versus accepting a single LLM candidate. Under a preregistered paired design (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Each pair used one shared LLM generation (shared_initial) that both conditions evaluated: baseline = accept single shot; guarded = validate and permit ≤1 automated repair. Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.996667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). The shared_initial estimand conditions on a single candidate per intent and therefore isolates validator/repair rescue effects for that candidate; under the supplied synthetic suite and model the baseline was near ceiling, limiting observable guarded marginality. We release the preregistration, full execution traces, and analysis artifacts for community follow‑up.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and configuration repair. Prior system and survey work documents tool‑augmented and verifier‑assisted architectures that reduce syntactic and semantic errors in specific settings, but reported benefits vary with model quality, task hardness, and validator design. This work addresses a focused operational question: does integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with a bounded automated‑repair budget) increase the probability that an LLM candidate passes semantic validation when both conditions evaluate the same candidate? We answer this using a preregistered paired confirmatory design that conditions on a single shared LLM draw per intent and therefore isolates the deterministic validator and repair mechanism’s effect on that candidate. Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) executed on N=300 paired intents with detailed artifact archival; (2) complete execution accounting showing near‑ceiling baseline performance for gpt-5-mini on the supplied synthetic suite and the resulting statistical interpretation; (3) an evidence‑grounded discussion of estimand choices, validator role, operational implications, and reproducibility requirements for follow‑up studies.
sections.related_work: Three converging literature threads motivate our design. First, multiple recent systems and surveys show active application of LLMs to NetOps problems (intent translation, configuration synthesis, repair) but emphasize prototype status and dataset/task heterogeneity. Representative works describe intent→configuration pipelines and template synthesis approaches and document varying absolute correctness rates across tasks. Second, planner‑centric and tool‑augmented frameworks (e.g., ReAct‑style, planner‑centric tool orchestration) enable LLMs to call validators and external tools; these architectures underpin proposed generate→validate→repair workflows. Third, verification and repair literature for configurations and code suggests hybrid approaches can reduce the incidence of syntactic and semantic errors, but results depend on verifier coverage and repair strategies. Our study complements these lines by preregistering a narrowly defined estimand (shared_initial candidate) and empirically measuring the deterministic validator’s rescue utility under that conditioning. The supplied verification/benchmarking literature shaped our preregistered choices: validator semantics (must_be_down_for_fields, workflow constraints) and task families (routing policy, ACL, VLAN/interface changes) reflect common NetOps correctness concerns documented in recent surveys and system reports.
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration: We froze a machine‑readable preregistration (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 above) before main execution. The confirmatory estimand (primary) is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) under a shared_initial protocol. Key preregistered design parameters: planned analyzable pairs N=300 (100 per complexity stratum: low/medium/high), single shared_initial LLM generation per pair, baseline = accept shared_initial as final, guarded = run deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with full_intent_constraint_validation on shared_initial and permit at most one automated repair call followed by revalidation. The preregistration targeted detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 with two‑sided α=0.05 and power≈0.8; a pilot (n=60) for discordance estimation was pre‑specified but was not executed (explicitly recorded; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed).
sections.results: Execution and accounting: The run completed all planned episodes. Execution manifest: started 2026-08-30T09:47:41Z, completed 2026-08-30T10:17:21Z; planned_episode_count=600, completed_episode_count=600, complete_pair_count=300, model_calls_used=301, stage_counts show shared_initial_generation=300 and repair=1. Condition margins (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes 299/300 (0.9966667), guarded successes 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory inference used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor: absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). Statistical note: the exact conditional McNemar approach conditions on m = n10 + n01 = 1 and uses a Binomial(m,0.5) reference; with a single discordant in one direction the two‑sided p equals 1.0, reflecting the extreme paucity of discordant evidence rather than evidence of equality. Per‑stratum outcomes are consistent with the margin: baseline — low 100/100, medium 100/100, high 99/100; guarded — 100/100 each (total 300/300).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: On the supplied synthetic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a single‑shot LLM candidate already satisfied the deterministic validator for 299/300 intents; consequently the guarded pipeline could improve only marginally under the shared_initial estimand. The single guarded‑only rescue demonstrates two operational points: (a) deterministic validators can catch specific workflow/order violations (here a must_be_down_for_fields sequencing omission) and (b) bounded automated repair can recover such ordering errors for the same candidate. However, the measured marginality depends on three interacting factors: base model capability (high for gpt-5-mini on this suite), task difficulty (the synthetic generator and per‑task workflow constraints used here), and the estimand conditioning (shared_initial vs. independent draws). Estimand choice consequence: the shared_initial design isolates the validator/repair effect for a fixed candidate but excludes any benefit that would arise from drawing alternative candidates for the guarded condition (we explicitly preregistered and executed this choice). Threats to validity: internal — single shared draw per pair, repair budget limited to ≤1, and single‑model evaluation; construct — the deterministic synthetic generator encodes workflow constraints that the validator checks (possible alignment between generator semantics and validator coverage); external — single LLM, single deterministic validator, and synthetic topologies limit generalisability to diverse production networks. Operational implications and recommendations: (1) when a base model is near‑ceiling on a target validator suite, marginal verifier utility for a shared candidate is small but guards retain value for auditing, explicit flagging, and targeted repairs; (2) to measure end‑to‑end pipeline gains allow independent candidate draws per condition or evaluate weaker models/real operator intents to increase discordance; (3) evaluate repair costs (latency, model calls) together with correctness to inform operational tradeoffs.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired study comparing a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + bounded automated repair) to accepting a single LLM candidate under a shared_initial estimand. For the supplied synthetic suite and gpt-5-mini, baseline single‑shot generation passed the deterministic validator in 299/300 cases and the guarded pipeline in 300/300 cases, producing a negligible paired improvement (0.00333; McNemar two‑sided p=1.0; 95% CI [0.00,0.01]). These results emphasize that verifier marginality is conditional on model strength, task hardness, validator coverage, and the estimand selected. We release the preregistration, full execution traces, and analysis artifacts to enable follow‑up studies that vary model strength, estimand (independent draws), validator diversity, and real‑world intent heterogeneity to better quantify practical operational gains from verifier‑assisted NetOps workflows.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/verifier‑diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reducing power to detect small absolute improvements relative to the preregistered target (10 percentage points).
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot (n=60) intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; main N=300 was used as pre‑specified without post‑hoc recalculation.
Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit when independent LLM draws per condition differ.

Repair transcript reporting: the archived run bundle contains the low‑level repair provider trace documenting the single automated repair and subsequent validation pass (recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl); the manuscript reports a concise archive‑traceable semantic summary of that repair rather than a verbatim transcript in the paper body.
